==Problem==

Barry wrote 6 different numbers, one on each side of 3 cards, and laid the cards on a table, as shown. The sums of the two numbers on each of the three cards are equal. The three numbers on the hidden sides are prime numbers. What is the average of the hidden prime numbers? 

<asy>
path card=((0,0)--(0,3)--(2,3)--(2,0)--cycle);
draw(card, linewidth(1));
draw(shift(2.5,0)*card, linewidth(1));
draw(shift(5,0)*card, linewidth(1));
label("$44$", (1,1.5));
label("$59$", shift(2.5,0)*(1,1.5));
label("$38$", shift(5,0)*(1,1.5));</asy>

<imath> \textbf{(A)}\ 13\qquad\textbf{(B)}\ 14\qquad\textbf{(C)}\ 15\qquad\textbf{(D)}\ 16\qquad\textbf{(E)}\ 17 </imath>

==Solution 1==

Let <imath>s</imath> be the sum of the two numbers on any card.  Then the hidden prime numbers are <imath>s-44</imath>, <imath>s-59</imath>, and <imath>s-38</imath>.

If <imath>s</imath> were even, then both <imath>s-44</imath> and <imath>s-38</imath> would be even, which is impossible since <imath>2</imath> is the only even prime number.

Therefore, <imath>s</imath> is odd. Since <imath>s-59</imath> is even and prime, <imath>s-59=2</imath> and thus <imath>s=61</imath>.  

Thus the hidden prime numbers are <imath>17</imath>, <imath>2</imath>, and <imath>23</imath>, so their average is <imath>\frac{17+2+23}{3}=\boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ 14}</imath>.

==Solution 2 (Answer Choices)==

Let <imath>x</imath> be the number on the other side of the card showing <imath>38</imath>.  Then the sum of the two numbers on each card is <imath>x + 38</imath>, so the number on the other side of the card showing <imath>59</imath> is <imath>x - 21</imath> while the number on the other side of the card showing <imath>44</imath> is <imath>x - 6</imath>.

Let <imath>a</imath> be the average of the hidden numbers.  Then <imath>a =\frac{1}{3}\left(x+(x-21)+(x-6)\right)=x-9</imath>, so <imath>x = a + 9</imath> and thus <imath>a + 9</imath> is prime.

Of the answer choices, only <imath>a = \boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ 14}</imath> yields a prime value of <imath>a + 9</imath>.

==Solution 3==
Say that the 3 hidden prime numbers are x, y and z for cards 1, 2, and 3 respectively. 
Therefore, since <imath>x+44 = z+38 = y+59</imath>, y=x-15, z=x+6. Now we note that if y is odd, then x must be even and z must be even too, which won't work since 2 is the only distinct even prime. Therefore, y must be even so y must be 2 so x=17, z=23 and the average is  <imath>\dfrac{42}{3}=\boxed{\textbf{(B)} 14}</imath>.
